## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.6 — it can leave the loopback now

> **Alpha.** Verified end to end against a real bridge on Linux, including the
> LAN and TLS paths below. Not tested on Windows or macOS, and the Android APK
> has still never run on a phone. For something that has actually been used in
> anger, stay on
> [v0.0.1](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/releases/tag/v0.0.1).

The listen address, authentication and TLS settings have existed since
[alpha.1](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/releases/tag/v0.0.2-alpha.1) while
deliberately doing nothing. They work now — which completes the original point
of all this: **running HueMux on a server as the one place light control
lives.**

```jsonc
{
  "profile": "lights",
  "listen": { "host": "0.0.0.0", "port": 7654 },
  "auth":   { "mode": "token", "token": "otter.beacon.willow" },
  "tls":    { "mode": "selfsigned" }
}
```

### Authentication

Required on every API call and WebSocket upgrade, as `Authorization: Bearer`
or `?token=` (a browser's WebSocket constructor cannot set headers, so the
query form is not optional). Three memorable words — generate one on the
settings page.

- **Connections from the machine itself are exempt**, so nothing about desktop
  use changes and you cannot lock yourself out of your own lights.
- **Failed attempts are rate limited** per source. A short memorable token is
  only defensible with a limiter in front of it, and that is deliberate rather
  than incidental.
- `/api/config` changes remain loopback-only even *with* a valid token.
  Rewriting the listen address or disabling auth should not be reachable from
  the network it governs.

### TLS

`selfsigned` generates and reuses a certificate — persisted, because a fresh
identity on every restart re-prompts every browser and is indistinguishable
from an attack. `files` uses a certificate you already have.

HueMux obtains nothing itself, which is what makes every sensible option work:
`tailscale cert` (least painful by a distance — auto-renewing, no port
forwarding, works off your LAN), a DNS-01 certificate for a domain you own, or
a local CA like mkcert.

A token over plain HTTP crosses the wire in cleartext, and HueMux tells you so
at startup instead of letting you discover it later.

### Fixes

- **The WebSocket origin check had dead code.** A comparison against `"[::1]"`
  could never match, because the URL parser strips the brackets first. `::1`
  was only ever accepted by accident of the literal beside it. The check now
  parses the address, which also covers the rest of `127.0.0.0/8`.
- **The server could not release its port.** There was no way to close the
  listener, so anything that started a server held the port until the process
  exited.
- **A self-signed certificate on a wildcard bind covered only loopback**, so
  every LAN browser would have hit a name mismatch stacked on top of the
  self-signed warning — useless for the one case that mode exists for. It now
  covers the machine's own addresses.

### Behaviour worth knowing

A port of `0` (the default) keeps the long-standing behaviour of scanning
upward from 7654 when the port is busy. An **explicitly configured** port now
binds strictly and fails if taken, because silently landing on a different
port than the one you wrote down is worse than a clear error.
